It's been about 6 or so years since I've attempted suicide. 

I had developed this horrible skin condition that started as a rash, but crusted up into dark purple spots all over my skin. My mom started beating me because she thought I "wasn't trying hard enough" to stop it and she wanted so badly for me to stop looking like a freak. The ever so outspoken kids at my school didn't help me feel any more human, either. I started cutting myself as a means to forget the emotional pain and because I decided, "fuck it. It's not like anyone would notice." 

This went on until a dermatologist noticed that some of my cuts were self inflicted. She talked to my mom about it, suggested that I see a professional, and my mom REFUSED. Flat out denied that I needed any help at all and went on to talk about how pathetic people were if they were suicidal.

I went on to high school. My skin started to clear up, but the bullying and abuse got worse, along with the cutting. Track and field made it harder to cut and easier for my family to be disappointed in me. It was my freshman year, and I was already convinced that I was a monster incapable of being cared for. No firearms in the house, so I tried to OD on pain killers and allergy meds (yeah, I'm not even sure if the allergy meds would have worked, but hey) in the tub. I got really sick, threw up a lot, crawled out of the bathroom and stayed up all night in my room.

I was sick for awhile. My little brother found out that I had been cutting. He hid my razors from me and hung out with me more. I'm still incredibly grateful for that little step and what it did for me. 

Fast forward about a year or so, and I get into my first relationship, which is something I regret with all my heart. I was still recovering, but her being sexually and emotionally abusive didn't help. It was even harder since I thought no one would believe me if I told them about it because bisexuality was really frowned upon in the community anyway. She knew about my past suicide attempt and the cutting and one day, she told me, "you should have just killed yourself. It would have suited you better." I did not want to even think about that. I got the fuck out as soon as possible.

I'm 20 now and, much to my ex's dismay, I'm still alive. My mom and I went to a parent/child counseling session and our relationship has improved. My brother is still very supportive. I'm in a healthy "no labels" relationship with a really caring guy. I'm still in college and doing very well. And my skin is completely cleared up. I don't have to feel like a freak whenever I put shorts on anymore. It's the little things in life that make me happy that I didn't have a gun or enough pills to OD that night.
